chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Hamza from Isma'il b. Abd al-Khaliq and Abi'l Sabah al-Kinani, together, from Abi Basir. He said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) saying:

Whoever withholds his harm from his neighbor, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will forgive his offense on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever purifies his stomach and his private parts will be a joyous king in paradise. And whoever frees a believing soul, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will build a house for him in paradise.

key_terms.أقاله: forgives/pardons his stumbling — used for overlooking faults
key_terms.محبورا: joyous, gladdened — a state of bliss in paradise
key_terms.نسمة مؤمنة: a believing soul — refers to freeing a Muslim slave

ai.seo_question: What are the three virtuous deeds that earn paradise according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) lists three virtuous deeds and their heavenly rewards: (1) withholding harm from one's neighbor earns forgiveness on the Day of Resurrection, (2) purity of stomach and private parts leads to being a joyous king in paradise, and (3) freeing a believing soul earns a house in paradise. This hadith was narrated in the assembly of the 11th of Rajab, 368 AH, emphasizing neighborly rights, self-restraint, and the merit of freeing slaves.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b `Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Abi Hamza from Isma`il b. `Abd al-Khaliq and Abi’l Sabah al-Kinani together from Abi Basir. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah (as) say:

Whoever withholds his harm from his neighbor, Allah will dismiss his offenses on the day of resurrection. Whoever is pure in his stomach and his private, he will be a joyous king in paradise. Whoever frees a believing soul, Allah builds a house for him in paradise.
